races.name: Tom McCormack Memorial Cup Maiden Hurdle
Massey Ferguson Johnston Farm Equipment Longford Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: King Of The Greys
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has faded in his last four starts including three over this identical 18-20f trip on Good ground; the finishing-fade flag is a significant concern in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to bring him into it late, and his 41-day absence adds further caution.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time after two 8ths and an unplaced run, though a fourth came five starts back. A 102 rating — second-best in this field — still makes him one of the leading dangers, but fitness following a 41-day break is the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Malbas
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, age 10, who will have this race to himself from the front — but his last nine runs show only two wins and four places, his form string reads 898-09, and he carries a finishing-fade warning; his role here is to set the race up rather than win it, and the STYLE_FIT flag confirms he may not relish the lead position he will be forced into.
runners_data.comment: Malbas already has today's trip and going under his belt, though his finishing positions have been modest across his last five starts. A rating of 106 — the best in this field — makes him the one to beat after a fair 24-day break.

runners_data.name: Whispering Willow
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer for Gavin Cromwell with a strong recent profile — 1-3-3 in his last five starts on Good ground, all over 16-20f — and an 18-day turnaround that suggests freshness; travels close to the pace and is the horse most likely to capitalise on Malbas's controlled front-running.
runners_data.comment: Whispering Willow won four starts back then added back-to-back thirds, before a below-par 6th last time. That form and experience over today's trip and going make her a leading threat, but the yard's recent cold spell (2 from 44) is the risk.

runners_data.name: Friar Hogan
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the ride on this five-year-old hold-up type who carries a tongue-tie and a finishing-fade concern; his best recent run was a second over 20f on Good ground but three subsequent blank efforts temper enthusiasm, and his natural rear-of-field style means he needs the pace to be stronger than Malbas is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Friar Hogan ran his best recent race when second last time out, that coming after being carried out and two unplaced efforts before it. Winless in his last five and 22 days off, he has today trip and going experience, but the patchy sequence keeps him mid-pack on our figures.

runners_data.name: I'm Flattered
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from Padraig Roche's yard who has been beaten between 6th and 8th in all five of his recorded runs; wearing a tongue-tie and pad, and his best going figures come on Yielding-Heavy rather than Good, making this surface a mild query.
runners_data.comment: I'm Flattered has yet to threaten in this sequence, without a finish better than 6th in her last five starts. She has experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 98 above her official mark of 92 hints at more to come.

runners_data.name: Burlington House
runners_data.note: A genuine rear-of-field operator by nature — bumped forward on the map because the hold-up cluster is overcrowded — who showed a strong second at 16f on Heavy ground but finds Good going considerably quicker than ideal; 67 days between runs is another note of caution for Oliver McKiernan's five-year-old.
runners_data.comment: Burlington House ran his best race last time, a close second, having been fourth and fifth in the two starts before. He carries experience over today's trip, but a 67-day absence and two unplaced efforts further back add uncertainty to his midfield claim.

runners_data.name: Circus Act
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue partners this seven-year-old who sports a hood and has finished 4th, 5th and 7th in his most relevant recent starts; tends to sit off the pace and does stay the trip, so if the race falls apart he is a potential beneficiary, but his Going record on Good is only modest.
runners_data.comment: Circus Act carries a rating of 100 — ten pounds above her official mark — and already has today's trip and going covered, marking her among the leading dangers. Recent finishes of 7th, 5th and 9th are modest, though, and a fall four starts back is a concern.

runners_data.name: Flash The Badge
runners_data.note: Five-year-old from John McConnell's yard who has returned 7th, 10th, 11th, 10th and 10th in his last five recorded runs, all on Good or Soft; 72 days off the track and a persistent finishing-fade flag make this a very difficult case to argue.
runners_data.comment: Flash The Badge is hard to fancy, managing only a 7th in his last five starts, with the yard also blank from 27 runners in the last fortnight. A 72-day absence adds to the concerns, though he does have experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Barrogstown Girl
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a reasonable record — two wins and five places in her career — ridden by apprentice Peter Smithers claiming 7lb; her last three runs read 6th, 8th and 17th but the form string shows she is better than that, and a clear run on the inside tracking Malbas could see her run into the places.
runners_data.comment: Barrogstown Girl remains lightly raced and unexposed, with 8th and 6th finishes and an unplaced effort in her recent starts. There's next to nothing to judge her on yet, but that inexperience means she could easily do better as she learns the game.

runners_data.name: Sneddy Eddie
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride on this Gordon Elliott six-year-old, but he is a genuine hold-up horse squeezed forward on the map by overcrowding at the rear; his last five runs on Good are unremarkable (5-5-13-26-21) and only ten days since his last run raises a small question about recovery, though Elliott's T14 record of 8/44 is notable.
runners_data.comment: Sneddy Eddie has managed no better than 5th in his last five starts, with three unplaced efforts in that sequence. He is fresh having run just 10 days ago and does have experience of today's going, but the modest form leaves him only a midfield chance.

runners_data.name: Demanding Gerry
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has finished 2nd four times in his last five starts on Good ground — all over 17-20f — making him arguably the most reliably placed horse in the field; his trainer Fahey has a quiet book but Demanding Gerry's profile of tracking the pace and grinding out a finish suits this race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Demanding Gerry has finished runner-up three times in her last five starts, a consistent record without a win. She was 4th last time out and does have experience over today's trip and going, form that keeps her firmly in this midfield mix.

runners_data.name: Movie King
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has not raced in 316 days — the longest layoff in the field by a substantial margin — and is a natural hold-up type that the map has pushed forward due to field overcrowding; his 2020 form showed a placed effort over 20f on Good but the lengthy absence and age make this a speculative entry at best.
runners_data.comment: Movie King returns from a 316-day absence, but his form includes back-to-back thirds two and three starts back. He has experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 96 well clear of his 84 mark hints at more once fitness allows.

runners_data.name: Dream Shaper
runners_data.note: Recent third on Good ground over 20f for I Madden is an encouraging recent run, and Paddy Cleary claims 7lb; wears a tongue-tie and is a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield by necessity, but if he can get a cleaner position than his style normally allows he is capable of running into the frame.
runners_data.comment: Dream Shaper was a solid third last time out, though that followed a fall three starts back among modest efforts. He has experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 97, well above his 82 mark, makes him worth another look.

runners_data.name: Dark Berkshire
runners_data.note: Rothwell's six-year-old holds a finishing-fade warning and has not bettered 7th in any of his last five starts on Good ground; wears a hood, is 21 days since last run, and is one of several horses here whose natural position at the rear of a 19-runner field may leave him with too much to do.
runners_data.comment: Dark Berkshire is hard to fancy, with a sequence reading unplaced, pulled up and no better than 7th across his last five starts. A rating of 77, just below his official mark, reflects that indifferent form, though he does have experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Finnicky Filly
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent racer who finished 5th, 6th and 5th in her most recent comparable runs on Good ground, with John Patrick Ryan saddling her 12 days after her last start; consistent enough without threatening to win, and the claiming jockey Kenneally taking 5lb helps the weight.
runners_data.comment: Finnicky Filly is yet to win but has been fairly consistent, finishing no better than 5th in her last five starts. She has experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 83, above her 76 mark, hints at a shade more in hand.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride on this eight-year-old, whose record of 1W-2P from 14 Good-ground runs includes a win at 16f but who was beaten 4th-6th-10th last time out; a natural hold-up type mapped forward by necessity, his best form came at shorter trips and the 2m3f is a stretch.
runners_data.comment: Surviving Murmansk won four starts back having been runner-up before that, but his last two runs have been a below-par pair of 6ths. He has experience of today's going, but on a rating of 78 he remains an outsider here.

runners_data.name: Il Pirata
runners_data.note: Reserve runner for Mrs Lorna Fowler with an unknown style tag, ridden by Reserve 1 jockey; has returned 6th, 7th, 6th and 8th in four recorded Good-ground starts and shows no win or place form — inclusion as a reserve means his impact on the race shape is contingent on late scratchings.
runners_data.comment: Il Pirata was brought down two starts back, otherwise racing in the 6th-8th range across his last five starts, form that leaves him fairly in the pack. He has experience of today's going, with a rating of 92 close to his 91 mark.

runners_data.name: Mambo Du Large
runners_data.note: Four-year-old reserve from Flannery's yard with only three hurdle runs to his name, all resulting in finishes of 6th, 7th and 13th; wears a tongue-tie and at age four over this trip in a 19-runner handicap he faces a significant test of experience if he gets a run.
runners_data.comment: Mambo Du Large remains unexposed, with a 6th his best effort in a mixed run that also featured an unplaced finish, a 7th and a race he failed to complete. He is fresh having run just 14 days ago, with more to find as he matures.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Ran just one day ago — by far the freshest turnaround in the field — and Hogan's seven-year-old carries a finishing-fade flag; won at 17f on Good as recently as his second-last start (form: P0-P18) but wore blinkers and is another reserve-jockey ride, making his participation conditional on scratchings, though the 1-day recovery makes him a query regardless.
runners_data.comment: Backinabit won two starts back but has otherwise found trouble, pulling up twice in his last five starts and finishing 8th when last seen. He has experience over today's trip and going, but a quick reappearance just a day later leaves him unproven on a rating of 83.

races.paceDynamic: Malbas is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing or able to press him from the front, he can control this race from the outset at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Kilbeggan. The pace will be honest but not frantic — a lone leader over 2m3f on a fair surface typically sets up a race that rewards horses who can travel prominently and quicken from the second-last hurdle rather than those who need a truly strong end-to-end gallop to close. The redistributed hold-up horses — Burlington House, Sneddy Eddie, Movie King, Dream Shaper, Dark Berkshire, Surviving Murmansk and Backinabit — are all genuine rear-of-field types who have been pushed forward on the map simply because there is no room for them all at the back; in reality, with only Malbas as a true front-runner, several of these will likely end up racing in a midfield cluster rather than off a true strong pace. Given one uncontested, sustainable pace-setter and a large field of prominent and hold-up types, this race shape strongly favours horses who can track Malbas close up in second or third and pounce turning for home — Whispering Willow, Demanding Gerry and Barrogstown Girl are best placed to exploit that position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Malbas Sets, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Malbas bowls along unchallenged and the field strings out behind, allowing prominent trackers to cruise into contention from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Malbas dictates a comfortable tempo, meaning the race only truly ignites in the final two flights where horses who have tracked him close-up carry the momentum; the prominent-to-midfield brigade get the ideal trip without burning energy chasing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Malbas is joined or briefly pressed early and the race becomes a true test of stamina, rewarding horses who can see out every yard of the 2m3f trip.
scenarios.body: A modest early battle or stumble in rhythm by Malbas can see the gallop become uneven, meaning only those with proven stamina and a prominent racing position survive the final climb; horses with strong staying form over 2m-plus on Good ground benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough in the final mile to bring a late finisher into play — and one of the true hold-up types manages to secure a better-than-expected position.
scenarios.body: This scenario is constrained by the sheer volume of hold-up horses in the field, most of whom will be further back than ideal and facing a traffic puzzle in a 19-runner handicap; only a horse that threads through late on a rail run has any realistic chance of catching the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Big-Field Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If a fall, a surge of pace from multiple positions early, or a significant incident reshuffles the field and neutralises the anticipated race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners over hurdles on a track that can compress fields into tight pockets, a chaotic race could see an unexpected horse land in front at a critical point and simply outstay a strung-out, disrupted field; lower-rated, resolute stayers with sound jumping records would benefit disproportionately.

watchPoints.text: Malbas sets a controlled, uncontested tempo — any horse that gets into second or third position early (Whispering Willow, Demanding Gerry) will be dangerously well-placed turning for home; watch whether anyone attempts to press the leader before the halfway point, as this would fundamentally alter the race shape.

With 19 runners over hurdles at Kilbeggan, traffic and interference at the early flights is a genuine risk — Jack Kennedy on Sneddy Eddie and Phillip Enright on Burlington House are experienced jockeys who will be trying to navigate their hold-up horses through a packed field, and any significant incident at a hurdle could shuffle the entire order.

Movie King's 316-day absence is the most extreme fitness concern in the race; if he runs and struggles to travel from the outset, he becomes an obstacle in a tightly packed field rather than a racing participant, which could impede those drawn around him.

Backinabit raced just one day ago — monitor declarations closely, as a horse with that turnaround is either in exceptional nick or being targeted at a specific mark, and if he does run the 1-day recovery window will attract scrutiny from the stewards' room if he underperforms sharply.

races.name: Massey Ferguson Johnston Farm Equipment Longford Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: High Notions
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for S G Carey ridden by claimer Michael Kenneally (5), twice placed on similar going from eight runs on Good, but the 40-day break and a recent form string showing back-of-the-field finishes demand improvement here at OR 99.
runners_data.comment: A third two starts back and experience over today's trip and going mark her as a leading threat. Yet to score in her last five starts, with a 40-day break and a below-par ninth three starts back among the main concerns.

runners_data.name: Fabhcun
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old (T14: 8/44, strong yard form) has failed to place in any of five recent starts, with no wins or places on Good ground from two tries, and the headgear change (cheekpieces) does little to inspire confidence after a 55-day layoff.
runners_data.comment: Fifth four and five starts back shows latent ability, and this is a further test over today's going. But he was pulled up last time out, and three starts back, with a 55-day layoff adding to the fitness doubts.

runners_data.name: Bowgate Street
runners_data.note: Philip Donovan rides this consistent seven-year-old who was placed four times in the last five on Good going from 15 outings on similar ground, and the 14-day turnaround for Flannery's yard (0/6 T14) is no concern given Bowgate Street clearly thrives racing fresh; a natural hold-up horse but form on this going is as strong as anyone's.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, having won four starts back, she boasts a solid recent scoreline, and she has already raced over today's trip and going. A below-par eighth three starts back is the blot, but a quick 14-day turnaround keeps her ticking over.

runners_data.name: O'Grady Cracker
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the ride on this four-year-old, but a stamina concern is flagged — the horse fades in the finish — and a 101-day absence combined with a form string of 9800- on similar going leaves little to work with off OR 94.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in his last two starts, with an eighth and ninth before that, and a 101-day absence, he has plenty to prove. Experience over today's trip and going helps his cause, but there is little in recent form to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Dearg Mor
runners_data.note: Peter Smithers (7) partners this five-year-old for Aidan Anthony Howard whose yard is 0/3 in the past 14 days; Dearg Mor has two fourth-place finishes in the last five on Good going but has not won and, while the trip (24f) suits recent form, the hold-up style works against him in a field this congested.
runners_data.comment: Fourth in each of his last two starts is a fair level, and he already has experience of today's going. An eighth three starts back and a winless run leave the form modest, with a 39-day gap since his last outing.

runners_data.name: Rare Times
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the mount on this lightly-raced four-year-old with an unknown running style designation (U) and just three runs on record; two of those came on Good ground without placing, and with so little data this is essentially an unknown quantity even with a top jockey.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out, and fifth three starts back either side of a seventh, she has shown only moderate form in a small sample. She does have experience of today's going, but a 77-day absence and a modest level make her hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Rizedda
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's six-year-old is flagged as fading in the finish and carries a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 after redistribution — a genuine hold-up type forced to race from further forward than ideal in this crowded field; five consecutive non-placings on Good going across six runs make the form hard to ignore, and the 49-day gap offers no obvious excuse.
runners_data.comment: A fourth three starts back is her best recent effort among finishes mostly outside the top six, and she has already raced over today's trip and going. Yet to score in her last five starts, a 49-day break adds to a moderate overall profile.

runners_data.name: Brianna Lily
runners_data.note: James Barcoe's nine-year-old returns just eight days after its last run — quick enough to suggest the handler has confidence — but this is a true hold-up horse in a field where the rear is overcrowded, meaning it is unlikely to get the position it needs; only two places from 15 runs on Good ground, and at OR 85 the profile is marginal.
runners_data.comment: A third four starts back stands out in a mixed sequence, and she has already raced over today's trip and going. Fourth just eight days ago, she is race-fit, though yet to score in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Lariat
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner for Liam Cusack, returning 17 days after last time, and with two places from 15 runs on Good over various trips; the 10-year-old's role here is tactical rather than winning, setting a tempo he can sustain without being pressured — his influence on the race shape outweighs his own winning prospects.
runners_data.comment: A fifth four starts back is his best recent form amid modest efforts, and he races over today's trip and going. Pulled up last time out, a quick 17-day turnaround offers a chance to bounce back from a workmanlike recent record.

runners_data.name: Patrick Street
runners_data.note: Daniel King rides this seven-year-old for Andrew Kinirons (T14: 1/5), who has a place on the board in the past fortnight; Patrick Street has won on Good ground and placed three times in nine, and while genuinely a hold-up horse reshuffled forward on the map due to field size, a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 suggests it may partially find its preferred position in a strung-out 19-runner field.
runners_data.comment: A third two starts back is the standout form line, and he already has experience of today's going. Sixth last time out, and yet to score in his last five starts, a 34-day gap adds to the questions.

runners_data.name: Laligurash
runners_data.note: Michael Griffin's four-year-old (T14: 0/0) is flagged as fading in the finish and carries a STYLE_FIT of 0.90; only three runs on record — all on Good, none resulting in a place — and a 49-day absence means this is lightly-exposed but in the wrong direction for a hold-up type shuffled closer than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Eighth last time out, with a seventh two starts back, is modest form, though two unseated efforts further back muddy the picture. He remains lightly raced and unexposed, so today's test could still bring improvement despite a 49-day absence.

runners_data.name: Little Boy Sivola
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell's five-year-old (T14: 2/22) wears a hood and the finish-fade flag compounds the redistribution issue — this true hold-up racer has seven runs on Good without a win or place and the pattern of mid-teen finishes suggests it lacks the class to compensate for a positional disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out is the pick of a modest sequence, and he races over today's trip and going. Yet to score in his last five starts, with three unplaced efforts in that span and a 41-day gap since his last run.

runners_data.name: Tawny Lea
runners_data.note: Thomas Coyle's six-year-old (T14: 0/4) has only three runs on record — one unknown position, one eighth, one twelfth — all on Good ground, all without placing; the finish-fade concern and genuine hold-up style finding itself mapped closer to the pace creates a compounding difficulty rather than an opportunity.
runners_data.comment: A refusal last time out followed an eighth and an unplaced run before that, leaving little hard form to judge. She remains lightly raced and unexposed, so there is room for improvement despite a 45-day absence.

runners_data.name: Thirsty Work
runners_data.note: Oliver McKiernan's five-year-old wears a tongue-tie and has been competitive on a variety of going but has finished no better than 10th in any of five recent starts on Good-adjacent conditions; genuinely a hold-up horse occupying a midfield slot it wouldn't choose, and a form line reading 0000-0 offers no encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in each of her last five starts, there is little recent form to work with, and a 57-day absence adds to the concerns. She does have experience over today's distance, but the overall picture makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Western Opera
runners_data.note: Kieran Callaghan's six-year-old (T14: 0/0) wears a tongue-tie and has four runs on Good going with one place — a second in a 22f Good contest — which is relevant form for this trip; as a hold-up horse pushed forward on the map, the STYLE_FIT of 0.92 leaves open the slight possibility it settles close enough in a messy 19-runner field to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: A second five starts back is by far her best effort, but a pulled-up run three starts back shows the inconsistency. Fourth last time out, she has experience of today's going, with a 22-day gap keeping her fresh but hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Bangor Lady
runners_data.note: Joshua Halford (7) takes the ride on this six-year-old for John Patrick Ryan (T14: 6/32, active yard); the finish-fade flag and five runs on Good without a place make this a difficult proposition, and the hold-up style in an overcrowded rear means it is unlikely to find clear daylight at the business end.
runners_data.comment: An eighth last time out continues a modest run of form, with two unplaced efforts and a fall also among her last five. She does have experience of today's going, but there is little in this recent sequence to inspire confidence after a 45-day break.

runners_data.name: Brohatna
runners_data.note: M M Rice's six-year-old is unridden (no jockey declared in data) and wears a tongue-tie; five from five recent starts on Good ground without a win — but placings at 4th and 5th in the last four suggest consistent competitiveness — and the trip range across recent runs (16f-22f) covers this 2m3f fine.
runners_data.comment: A fourth two starts back and experience over today's trip and going head this field's recent form. A brisk 20-day turnaround keeps him fresh, and despite being yet to score in his last five starts, he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Lakewood Rose
runners_data.note: Miss Niamh Carol Hennessy's eight-year-old (no jockey declared) is the only genuine prominent runner behind Lariat, returning 14 days after last time; eight recent runs on Good ground with one place, a consistent record of landing in the 3-7 range, and a prominent style that allows this mare to track Lariat and apply pressure — the race's key tactical figure after the front-runner itself.
runners_data.comment: A third two starts back underlines her claims, backed by fourths three and four starts back, making her a leading danger, despite a below-par seventh last time out. She has already raced over today's trip and going, with a brisk 14-day turnaround keeping her fresh.

runners_data.name: Light Her Up
runners_data.note: Hugh Paul Finegan's eight-year-old returned just three days ago — an unusually quick turnaround — and while it has placed on Good ground (4th and 6th in recent runs), this genuine hold-up horse is mapped to midfield due to the overcrowded rear; the rapid reappearance is either confidence or opportunity-seeking, but the positional challenge remains.
runners_data.comment: A fourth four starts back is her best recent effort, with two sixths and an unplaced run since. She races just three days after her last outing, and does have experience of today's going, though the recent sequence is workmanlike rather than progressive.

races.paceDynamic: Lariat is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner field and, crucially, faces no meaningful speed threat to his lead — Lakewood Rose is the only prominent type, and with nothing else to press Lariat from the front, the pace is likely to be sustainable rather than scorching. Over 2m3f on Good ground at Kilbeggan, a controlled lead at honest fractions over 14 flights sets up a strongly run race that will be decided on stamina and jumping ability in the home straight, rather than a sprint finish off a slow tempo. The lone-leader scenario is therefore the dominant shape: horses who can travel just off the pace and pick Lariat off from the second-last flight hold the clearest tactical advantage, while true hold-up horses face a particular challenge in this field. A large number of the hold-up runners — Rizedda, Brianna Lily, Laligurash, Little Boy Sivola, Tawny Lea, Thirsty Work, Bangor Lady, Western Opera, and Light Her Up — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is overcrowded with genuine hold-up types; in a race where Lariat dictates an uncontested lead, none of these horses are likely to secure the ground they truly need to express their best form, and the profile that benefits most clearly is the prominent-to-mid racer who can track the pace, travel with minimal effort, and pounce once Lariat flattens on the run-in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lariat Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Lariat bowls along in front at his own tempo and the midfield cluster tracks without drama, setting up a stamina test from two out.
scenarios.body: Lariat, unhurried in front, delivers a controlled pace that suits horses travelling prominently and jumping fluently, reducing the race to a grinding test on the run-in where cruising speed into the straight counts most; Lakewood Rose, tracking just off the pace, and Bowgate Street, who handles this going well across 15 runs, are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Burst From Tracking Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just honest enough to string the field out but not punish those coming from slightly off the pace, allowing midfield movers to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Horses who settle mid-division with cover and then pick up on the long Kilbeggan run-in can close down a tiring Lariat, rewarding those with genuine finishing energy on Good ground; Brohatna, consistent at this sort of trip on Good going across all five recent starts, and High Notions, placed twice on similar ground, have the profile to arrive late with purpose.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Lakewood Rose pushes Lariat for the lead from an early stage, cranking up the tempo and turning this into a true test of jumping speed and stamina.
scenarios.body: A contested front creates a more pressured gallop that burns off horses who haven't settled efficiently, leaving the spoils to whichever of the prominent pair jumps better or to an alert midfield horse who sits third and benefits from the duel; Lakewood Rose, who has placed prominently and handles Good ground across eight recent runs, is best positioned to survive her own pressure-setting role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Large Field
scenarios.trigger: If the 19-runner field produces interference, fallers, or a badly disrupted gallop that fragments the race into segments, rewarding fluent jumpers who find daylight early.
scenarios.body: In a messy, disorganised renewal the premium falls on horses that jump cleanly and quickly find their own rhythm rather than being shuffled around by congestion; Patrick Street, who has won on Good going and showed a placed effort at this sort of trip, and Western Opera, consistent in similar conditions across nine recent outings, could emerge from the chaos with clean passages.

watchPoints.text: Lariat's pace judgement is critical — if Brian Hayes allows the tempo to drop significantly in the back straight, the large midfield pack will compress and the tactical advantage of tracking close to the leader will be neutralised, potentially gifting the race to the fastest finisher rather than the best traveller.

With 19 runners over 14 hurdles at Kilbeggan, the risk of a pile-up or interference at an early flight is elevated — monitor the draw and early positions carefully, as any runner caught wide or boxed in from the off faces a near-impossible task getting competitive.

runners_data.name: In The Trenches
runners_data.note: Cromwell and Donoghue combine in strong form (2/44 T14); prominent style fits the shape perfectly, has placed seven times in 15 similar-going runs and won once, giving him strong each-way claims if he travels smoothly behind Magic Day.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back, and a podium three starts back, mark him a leading danger, with experience over today's trip and going. He was pulled up last time out, though, and the yard is out of form at just 5% in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Magic Day
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who shapes as pace-setter; De Bromhead T14 of 6/41 is encouraging, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) is relevant only if something forces her off the front — on her own terms she dictates.
runners_data.comment: A third two starts back is her standout effort in this field, and she has already raced over today's trip and going. Sixth last time out, and yet to score in her last five starts, a 41-day absence adds to the concerns.

runners_data.name: Laxxio
runners_data.note: Anthony Mullins/Danny Mullins combination running off a 20-day break; travels prominently which suits the shape, and his three Good-ground runs include two thirds, though his hurdles form is largely on Soft/Heavy and the going switch invites a query.
runners_data.comment: Thirds two and four starts back show him at a consistent level, with experience of today's going. Fourth last time out, and fresh on a brisk 20-day turnaround, he gets the nod for us on that overall profile, despite a pulled-up effort three starts back.

runners_data.name: Andys Flame
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type who won over 20f on Good 41 days ago; tongue strap fitted, and the claiming jockey Shane Fitzsimons (7lb) helps offset his OR-105 burden — needs pace to collapse in front of him, which is not guaranteed with Magic Day controlling.
runners_data.comment: A win four starts back is the standout form line, and he has already raced over today's trip and going. Below that level since, unplaced last time out, with the yard cold at 0% over the last fortnight the main risk.

runners_data.name: In For The Night
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with a deceptive form string (008-7), though he has two wins and four places in 15 Good-ground starts; Conor O'Dwyer's son Charlie (3lb claim) rides, but recent runs have been modest and he looks one to frame rather than win.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out continues a moderate sequence, with an eighth and two unplaced efforts also in his last four starts. He does have experience over today's trip and going, though little in this recent form suggests major improvement after a 49-day break.

runners_data.name: Silly Mongoose
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a hood and tongue strap; won over 16f on Good 22 days ago, but the step up to 19f in trip is unproven — if the extra distance suits, a late run from off the pace is plausible on a clean jumping round.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back is the clear highlight, though he was unplaced last time out, and again four starts back, a mixed picture. He does have experience over today's trip and going, with a brisk 22-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: You Done Well
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose instinct is to be close to the pace, but with Magic Day, In The Trenches, Laxxio, and In For The Night ahead of him, he's likely to find himself further back than ideal; the STYLE_FIT discount applies and his chance depends on circumstances forcing a reshuffle.
runners_data.comment: Thirds in each of his last two starts, and a second four starts back, mark him out as solid, with experience over today's trip and going. Yet to score in his last five starts, though a brisk 21-day turnaround keeps him fresh.

runners_data.name: Mon Sheriffe
runners_data.note: Has fallen, pulled up, and unseated in recent form (6P6P-U); a genuine prominent type who lacks the firepower to secure that position in this field and has no wins or places from 13 similar-going runs — the redistribution compounds an already modest profile.
runners_data.comment: Unseated last time out continues a difficult run that also features two pulled-up efforts in his last five starts, leaving little hard form to trust. He does have experience over today's trip and going, but a 49-day absence and this sequence make him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Tudorista
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse running off a sharp 14-day turnaround for Edward Power; all five Good-ground starts have produced placed finishes (fourth or worse) with no win, and without a bold jumping round he is likely to find the principals beyond him.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, and fourth five starts back, are the high points either side of a ninth and eighth, a modest overall level. She does have experience over today's trip and going, on a brisk 14-day turnaround, but the recent form remains unremarkable.

runners_data.name: Marlpark
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago — the most recent runner in the field — and has fallen in his last start; blinkers fitted, a true hold-up type shuffled into a midfield map position, and the combination of fatigue risk, STYLE_FIT tag, and jumping concerns makes him difficult to support.
runners_data.comment: A fall last time out followed a pulled-up run before that, with a fourth three starts back marking his best recent form. He does have experience over today's trip and going, but a run of modest finishes and a three-day turnaround make him hard to trust.

races.paceDynamic: Magic Day is the one confirmed front runner and, with Kilbeggan's Good ground placing no premium on extreme early speed, she can dictate a controlled, measured gallop that never truly tests the field's stamina. In The Trenches, Laxxio, and In For The Night are genuine prominent types who will track directly behind her, creating a compact leading group through the early stages rather than any breakneck pace. The field actually contains more prominent types than the race shape can comfortably absorb — You Done Well and Mon Sheriffe are natural prominent racers who will be squeezed back into midfield against their instincts, which compromises their chances in any scenario requiring that position. A sustainable front-running tempo on Good ground at Kilbeggan's 2m3f trips historically produces a strongly run race relative to clock but not attritional, meaning horses who travel prominently close to the pace without burning early energy — particularly those with strong Good-ground form — hold the decisive tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Magic Day Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Day is allowed to bowl along at her own rhythm unchallenged from the front, dictating a true but not punishing pace throughout.
scenarios.body: She sets a sustainable tempo that suits the prominent types tracking her, and no one applies meaningful pressure until the final circuit, leaving her rivals unable to mount a coordinated challenge. In The Trenches and Laxxio, ideally placed just off her, are best positioned to capitalise if she tires late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If In The Trenches or Laxxio move smoothly alongside Magic Day approaching the last two hurdles and the front runner finds her effort flattening.
scenarios.body: The Cromwell/Donoghue combination on In The Trenches carries notable in-running form on Good ground, and Laxxio's Danny Mullins partnership is capable of producing a well-timed challenge. Both sit perfectly placed to pounce without covering extra ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely testing and the front-running group ties up in the final half mile, opening a gap for a sustained finisher.
scenarios.body: Andys Flame has won over this sort of trip on Good ground and, ridden by a claiming jockey, benefits from a weight pull; Silly Mongoose, who won over 16f on Good, could also close with purpose if the tempo sustains. True hold-up profiles are limited here, so this scenario requires an unusually strong pace from Magic Day.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Congested Midfield Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the squeezed-out prominent types — You Done Well and Mon Sheriffe — cause traffic and interference in the midfield pack, creating a messy race that rewards a horse who avoids trouble.
scenarios.body: Mon Sheriffe and You Done Well, pushed back against their natural instincts, may unsettle the midfield rhythm and produce a race where a horse tracking wide and clean benefits disproportionately. Both carry STYLE_FIT discounts and their out-of-role positioning makes this scenario genuinely low probability.

watchPoints.text: Magic Day sets off in front — if Laxxio or In The Trenches press her sooner than expected turning for home, the race could quicken sharply and catch hold-up types flat-footed.
Marlpark ran only three days ago and fell on his last outing; watch for any signs of jumping hesitation early that could cause interference for horses tracking behind him.

You Done Well and Mon Sheriffe are both natural prominent types who cannot get their preferred position — monitor how they settle in the opening half mile, as restless, unbalanced running could disrupt the midfield group.

Andys Flame's claiming jockey Shane Fitzsimons takes 7lb off his back, which is a meaningful weight concession at this level on Good ground — if the pace genuinely tests the front runners, he is the most likely beneficiary from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Giorgia Rose
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins's six-year-old wears a hood and tongue-tie and is a genuine hold-up horse whose strong-pace requirement makes this steady-gallop race shape unfavourable; the redistribution to midfield reflects the overcrowded rear of the field, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers optimism — three Good-ground runs show consistent top-three finishes in form but the tactical mismatch is real.|

races.paceDynamic: Le Questionnaire is the confirmed front-runner here and, with just one genuine pace-setter in a nine-runner field over 3m½f at Kilbeggan on Good ground, he is set to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable, unhurried tempo. Jack Kennedy will look to dictate on Le Questionnaire, and with no confirmed challenger to push him from the outside, the early gallop is unlikely to be fierce — this shapes as a genuinely steadily-run maiden hurdle that will be decided by a stamina test in the final half-mile. Giorgia Rose is a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains more genuine hold-up horses than can all settle at the rear in the same race; she is unlikely to secure a true back-of-the-field pitch. The sustainable pace, long trip, and Good ground combine to favour prominent racers who can travel comfortably close to Le Questionnaire's measured gallop and pick up when it matters, rather than hold-up horses who need a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace, Prominent Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Le Questionnaire controls the tempo unchallenged and the race is truly run to suit those travelling prominently throughout.
scenarios.body: Le Questionnaire sets a steady, honest clip over the marathon trip and the horses closest to him — those with the stamina and tactical fluency to sit just off the pace — are primed to pounce approaching the last; horses with prominent style profiles and proven Good-ground form over staying trips benefit most from this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stamina War, Late Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly quickens from halfway and the front group ties up in the closing stages, allowing true hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: A genuine early injection of pace — perhaps Clone Cross or Barton Sky pushing more aggressively — would stretch the field and create the gruelling 3m½f slog that suits horses arriving late on the bridle; Installment or Lord Lackendarra, both hold-up types with staying-trip profiles, could capitalise if the front horses stop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Bolts Up
scenarios.trigger: If Le Questionnaire's tactical ride translates into a clean break at the final hurdle with enough left to hold on unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Kennedy dictates on the bridle throughout and when he asks Le Questionnaire to quicken coming off the final bend, the controlled fractions mean he has a well-preserved tank; despite the STYLE_FIT flag, if the race truly falls perfectly to Le Questionnaire's front-running strengths, this well-connected Elliott runner punches above his redistribution discount.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses compete for the lead, the race falls apart tactically and a fresh-travelling hold-up horse catches all rivals flat-footed.
scenarios.body: A scrappy contested gallop over this extreme trip on Good ground can undo even strong travellers — if the pace becomes uneven and the field strings out early, Rusty Harkness (De Bromhead, good form figures at this trip, recent second) or Lord Lackendarra emerges from the carnage with a late run that the muddled pace has created.

watchPoints.text: Le Questionnaire's unchallenged control of the tempo is the race's pivot — if Kennedy is allowed to dictate at will, every hold-up horse is immediately at a disadvantage; watch for any early pressure from Clone Cross or Barton Sky that could disrupt the front-runner's rhythm.

Clone Cross's high frequency of falls and pull-ups (F, F, P in recent form) is a safety and race-shape concern — his jumping must be monitored from the outset, as a departure from the lead group could materially alter the pace map.

Lord Lackendarra's finishing positions have deteriorated sharply (6th, 3rd, 2nd → 6th, 0th) and he debuts in headgear today — watch how the hood affects his early behaviour and whether Dylan Whelan can settle him in a field of genuine hold-up types all seeking the same ground.

Giorgia Rose's true hold-up profile is masked by her midfield map position — if Good ground and Kilbeggan's track configuration allow her to drift back to her natural pitch, watch whether she gets the strong pace she needs to make her trademark late rattle meaningful over 3m½f.

Barton Sky's 425-day absence makes his condition entirely opaque — watch the paddock closely and monitor whether Harry Sexton (7) can settle the eight-year-old early, as a fresh horse after such a lengthy break can either overrace badly or produce a career-best first-time back.

runners_data.name: Garnacho
runners_data.note: Prominent type with two wins and five places in similar going, ran 1st and 2nd in last two Good-ground starts over 20f, light claimer Thomas O'Connor rides, headgear (hg:t) consistent, 24 days fresh — profiles as the most dangerous pressing horse behind Linden Arden.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and second two starts back, but two well-beaten efforts and an unplaced run further back cloud the picture. Carries a big 170 lb and sits ninth of twelve on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Linden Arden
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner here though her STYLE_FIT of 0.93 flags she has run prominently rather than in a strict lead role; won over 19f on Good, 124-day absence is a significant concern for fitness, but Kelly has one winner from 12 in the last 14 days.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up three starts back, and a winner four starts back, show solid recent form, and he has run over today's trip and going before. Second of twelve on our figures, though a break of 124 days since that run is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Milan Forth
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a win and two places in 11 Good-ground runs, suited by this trip having placed twice over 20f on Good, headgear (tp) steady, 39 days since last run is not alarming, seven-pound claimer Kevin Healy adds interest.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up two starts back stands out on an otherwise modest sheet, and he has run over today's trip and going before. Yet to win in his last five starts, but a rating of 123 puts him third of twelve in this field.

runners_data.name: Costacurta
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's in-form yard (6/41 last 14 days) sends this six-year-old who has placed in five of six Good-ground starts, the most recent being a second and two thirds; prominent style on a track and going he clearly handles well is a strong combination.
runners_data.comment: Consistently in the frame with a second and three thirds in his last five starts, but yet to win there. Has run over today's trip and going before, and sits eighth of twelve on a rating of 117.

runners_data.name: Rexem

runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse aged 11 who has run exclusively on Good ground in his recent history (15/15), consistently places in the four-to-five range without winning; headgear (t) unchanged, 60-day absence is a mild concern for an ageing horse.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back is the big form pointer, and he has run over today's trip and going before. He's rated a table-topping 128 here, though a pulled-up run in that sequence and a 60-day layoff add some risk.

runners_data.name: Freddie Robdal
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose crowded position in this field means he is unlikely to secure that spot — bumped into midfield territory on the map; De Bromhead trainer angle is always live, and Good-ground form (12/15) is solid, but the style squeeze tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Two runner-up efforts further back in this sequence are the form high points, but a pulled-up run and an unplaced effort since suggest question marks. Rated bottom of the twelve runners here on a figure of 109, and he'll need to find more.

runners_data.name: Prince Palace
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose entire recent form history comes on Soft or Heavy ground, not a single recent run on Good — going concern is genuine here; three question-mark finishes (pulled up) in the last five runs, and this is a step into unfamiliar conditions.
runners_data.comment: A stack of substandard efforts litters his recent form, including two pulled-up runs and two runs finishing ninth. He has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 118 sits well above his official mark of 109, leaving him sixth of twelve.

runners_data.name: Grange Walk
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse who fancies a stronger pace than this race is likely to offer; the field congestion means he will struggle to get to the rear in his own time, with his midfield repositioning reducing the value of his natural finishing style on this Good ground.
runners_data.comment: A third two starts back is the standout form line, with a fourth and a fifth also among his recent finishes. He has run over today's trip and going before and is race-fit with a run just 12 days ago; rated 118, he's seventh of twelve here.

runners_data.name: Golden Temple
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's six-year-old is another hold-up type displaced from his natural position by field density, with a STYLE_FIT of 0.91; form figures of 9,6,6,10,9 on recent starts show no win or place threat, and Good-ground form (10/15 runs) has not produced a placed effort.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent sequence including two ninths offers little to work with, though a fourth last time out is a small step forward. He has run over today's trip and going before and is rated 110, eleventh of twelve here.

races.paceDynamic: Linden Arden is the one confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field, and with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge, she is expected to bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated tempo on good ground over 2m4½f at Kilbeggan. That sustainable gallop will suit horses who can travel prominently just behind her and pounce in the straight, rather than those requiring a truly strong pace to close into. Garnacho, Milan Forth, and Costacurta are all natural prominent types who should settle comfortably in second rank, making this a race dominated by the front two or three positions from start to finish. This race shape squarely favours hold-up-to-prominent horses who can travel in the first three or four and have the stamina to grind Linden Arden down, rather than genuine deep closers who need fractions to be run in front of them. Note that the field contains more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate naturally — Freddie Robdal, Grange Walk, and Golden Temple are genuine pace/hold-up horses who are unlikely to secure their preferred positions in this competitive configuration, and Linden Arden is most likely to dictate, with Garnacho and Costacurta best placed to press from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Linden Arden controls, prominent raiders strike
scenarios.trigger: If Linden Arden leads uncontested and the prominent horses behind her travel comfortably into a steady gallop.
scenarios.body: Linden Arden sets an uncontested, manageable tempo and the race effectively becomes a stamina test from three out, where horses like Garnacho, Costacurta, and Milan Forth, all travelling handy, have the ideal platform to overhaul her in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, hold-up horses ambush
scenarios.trigger: If Linden Arden's front-running tactics produce an uncharacteristically slow early pace that results in a sprint finish from the last.
scenarios.body: A dawdling tempo could compress the field and allow genuine hold-up types like Rexem or Tullybeg, who have strong going form on good ground, to produce a late rattle that catches the prominent horses flat-footed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Linden Arden cuts loose, soft win
scenarios.trigger: If Linden Arden is allowed to get into a rhythm and the chasing pack is disorganised or slow to respond to her lead.
scenarios.body: Racing confidently in front with no pressure, Linden Arden could exploit a fractured chasing group and simply outstay the field over this stamina-demanding 2m4½f trip on good ground, her one win having come over 19f on good.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and attrition, outsiders profit
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fences cause trouble and the race breaks down into an error-strewn lottery with significant carnage in the field.
scenarios.body: A high-incident race reduces the advantage of tactical nous and class, opening the door for Clonbury Bridge or Tullybeg, both proven stayers with strong good-ground form across multiple runs at this type of trip.

watchPoints.text: Watch Linden Arden's jumping from the front — if she makes an early error under Harry Sexton (7), a 124-day absence could manifest and collapse the race shape entirely, leaving the contest wide open for the prominent trio behind.

Garnacho's claimer Thomas O'Connor (7) will need to position him efficiently in the first two furlongs given the number of prominent types; if Garnacho gets shuffled back at the start, his chance is materially reduced in what is expected to be a slow-tempo race.
Prince Palace has no recent form on Good ground — every run in the last five came on Soft or Heavy — and should be monitored for distress in the middle stages if the track rides faster than expected.

Rexem ran just 14 days ago; watch in the parade ring for signs of freshness or fatigue — if travelling sweetly through the early stages, his Good-ground record over this trip makes him a potential wide-market mover late.

The three redistributed horses — Freddie Robdal, Grange Walk, and Golden Temple — will be worth tracking in the first half-mile to see how much pace congestion actually materialises; if any of them do get a clear prominent position, the scenario probabilities shift meaningfully.

runners_data.comment: A runner-up four starts back is the clear high point in a moderate recent sequence that includes two unplaced efforts. She has run over today's trip and going before and is fairly fresh on a 20-day break, rated 92 and seventh of seventeen here.

runners_data.comment: Two runner-up efforts three and four starts back are the clear form high points, and she has run over today's trip and going before. Rated 91 and eighth of seventeen, though an unplaced run last time out and a pulled-up effort further back temper the claims.

runners_data.name: Island McCoo
runners_data.note: Two wins and two places from five runs on Good ground underline how well this type of surface suits him; ran just 14 days ago off an OR of 88 and showed form figures of 1 and 2 over course-relevant distances — prominent style ideally placed to profit from a controlled tempo.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back, and a runner-up three starts back, show he has ability, but two runs finishing eighth, including last time out, cloud the picture. He has run over today's trip and going before; rated 87, he's thirteenth of seventeen here.

runners_data.name: My Policy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with an excellent strike rate on Good ground (12 from 13 runs), placed four times without winning recently; ran 20 days ago and the blinkers are on — the question is whether he can convert those placed efforts in a competitive 17-runner field.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up two starts back is the standout effort in an otherwise mixed recent sequence that includes two pulled-up runs. She has run over today's going before and is fairly fresh on a 20-day break, rated 89 and tenth of seventeen here.

runners_data.name: Watty Show
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse carrying a fades-in-finish flag, shifted into the midfield map position because the rear of this field is structurally overcrowded — his 0W0P record on Good ground (six runs) and no wins at any going in this distance range make him hard to strongly support; De Bromhead's yard is in form (6/41 T14) but the positional compromise is real.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent sequence including two sevenths and a pulled-up run offers little encouragement, though she has run over today's going before. Rated 79 here and sixteenth of seventeen, she has plenty to find on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Ferdia
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old natural hold-up type placed into midfield only due to the volume of hold-up horses in the field; ran just seven days ago and his form figures over Good ground show consistent mid-pack finishes without threatening — the redistribution makes a winning run structurally harder to deliver.
runners_data.comment: He tops this field on our figures with a rating of 113, a striking 29 lb clear of his official mark of 84, and he has run over today's trip and going before. His recent finishes have been modest, but fresh off a run just seven days ago and with that scale of edge, he rates the one to beat.

runners_data.name: My Good Pal
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with one win and four places from Good-ground starts; a course-specific entry for Gavin Cromwell's yard and ran 21 days ago — form figures include a second over 3m and Good-ground placing at 2m4f, giving him the trip credentials needed here.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up three starts back is the one bright spot in an otherwise indifferent recent sequence that also features an unseated run. He has run over today's trip and going before, but the yard is out of form at just a 5% strike rate from its last 44 runners; rated 86, he's fourteenth of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Ixigreczed
runners_data.note: A fades-in-finish hold-up horse with 0W0P from fifteen Good-ground runs, placed in midfield by necessity rather than by profile; headgear (blinkers) is in play and the trainer has no recent winners — raw form and structural position both work against him.
runners_data.comment: A consistently modest recent sequence with a best of fifth offers little to shout about, though she has run over today's trip and going before. Our rating of 88, a touch above her official mark of 81, has her twelfth of seventeen here.

runners_data.name: Kilashee
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old hold-up horse who was pulled up twice in recent starts; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that he is operating outside his natural rear position, though his Good-ground sim record shows placed efforts including a win — age and recent form make it hard to envisage a winning run.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back pulled-up efforts in her last two starts are hard to overlook, though she has run over today's trip and going before and races fresh on a seven-day turnaround. Our rating of 90, well above her official mark of 80, sees her ninth of seventeen despite that recent blip.

runners_data.name: Battle Of Benburb
runners_data.note: Prominent-style gelding returning from a lengthy 109-day break for a small yard; his course form (three places from five runs on Good) and tongue-tie suggest connections are positive, but the layoff is a meaningful risk in a 17-runner handicap at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Four pulled-up efforts in his last five starts make for a difficult formline to trust, though he has run over today's trip and going before. Our rating of 93 sits well clear of his official mark of 79, sixth of seventeen here, but a 109-day absence adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Love Like This
runners_data.note: Consistent record showing three wins and four places from eight Good-ground starts, and ran just seven days ago for the busy John Patrick Ryan yard; the prominent style and reliable form figures (3,4,1,3 in last four completed) make this one of the more profile-appropriate runners for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, give her solid recent claims, and she has run over today's trip and going before. Rated 85 and fifteenth of seventeen despite that formline, she races fresh having run just seven days ago.

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse with headgear (blinkers) and a 7-day turnaround for John Joseph Hanlon; Good-ground sim record is modest (seven runs, zero wins, one place) and no jockey is listed — an absentee rider flag in a 17-runner field adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent sequence including a fall and two unplaced efforts offers little on pure form, though he has run over today's trip and going before. Our rating of 96, well clear of his official mark of 88, has him fifth of seventeen, but the yard is running at a 0% strike rate from its last 23 runners.

runners_data.name: Walkmethroughit
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type with a fades-in-finish flag, returning from 134 days off for a trainer with no recent winners; his sim-going record on Good is particularly thin (two runs, no places) and the lengthy absence compounds the concern — the repositioning into midfield reflects field congestion, not an upgrade in role.
runners_data.comment: Two pulled-up efforts either side of a pair of sevenths and an eighth make for a poor recent sequence, and there's been no run for 134 days since. Rated bottom of the field here on a figure of 76, he has a great deal to prove.

runners_data.name: Mercurial Sea
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who should secure an uncontested lead in this field; five career runs yield four placings on Good ground, and at 5yo with a fresh 10-day turnaround, the key question is whether he can maintain his advantage over an extended 2m4½f trip — the step up from his recent 2m flat form is the primary concern, and the STYLE_FIT tag notes a slight positional mismatch in what is a very open handicap.
runners_data.comment: Two runner-up efforts sit either side of a couple of well-beaten runs in a mixed recent sequence, and she has run over today's trip and going before. Our rating of 89 is a touch below her official mark of 94, leaving her eleventh of seventeen, though she is race-fit on a 10-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Mercurial Sea is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-horse handicap chase and, with no genuine challenger for the lead likely to materialise, should be able to dictate an honest but sustainable gallop around Kilbeggan's flat, turning track over 2m4½f on Good ground. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Watty Show, Walkmethroughit, Ferdia, Ixigreczed, and Kilashee are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions simply because the rear of the field cannot accommodate them all — meaning the genuine closers will be squeezed together and competing for the same ground late on. The prominent runners sitting just off Mercurial Sea's shoulder — Hurricane Honey, Island McCoo, My Policy, My Good Pal, Battle Of Benburb, and Love Like This — are therefore in the tactically privileged zone: close enough to strike when it matters, far enough back to avoid the early burn. The race shape strongly favours the genuine prominent-to-midfield types who can travel smoothly in a mid-pack position and pick off a tiring field over the final two fences, with true hold-up horses at a structural disadvantage given the compressed rear and the controlled, uncontested pace being set.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mercurial Sea Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Mercurial Sea sets his own uncontested rhythm and the prominent pack cannot sustain a challenge from the second-last fence.
scenarios.body: Mercurial Sea dictates a measured pace from the front, conserving enough energy to find extra when challenged at the business end; on Good ground at Kilbeggan, a front-runner who has set a sustainable tempo is hard to reel in late in this field. The prominent horses best placed to chase are those with genuine pace figures — Island McCoo and Love Like This have the profiles to be closest, but they must still bridge the gap against a horse in rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Mercurial Sea begins to weaken from the second-last and the prominent horses travelling smoothly surge past in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Island McCoo, Love Like This, and Hurricane Honey are all prominent-style horses with strong records on Good ground and this trip, ideally positioned to pounce when the front-runner's advantage dissolves inside the final half-mile. Love Like This in particular has consistent placed form at this trip and going combination, and My Good Pal brings course-form credentials that suit a race run at a controlled pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Raider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string out the field and one of the genuine midfield horses produces a sustained run from three out.
scenarios.body: My Policy and My Good Pal, both rated prominent-to-midfield and with solid Good-ground form, could be the beneficiaries if the gallop quickens sufficiently to expose the front-runner early; the flat Kilbeggan track gives a sustained railing runner a chance to peg back leaders without needing a sharp turn of foot. Battle Of Benburb, with a placed record on this course and going, is another whose patient style could pay off if traffic clears.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final mile and a compressed group of redistributed hold-up horses manage to thread through in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Watty Show, Ferdia, or Luimneach to overcome their out-of-role positioning in a field where the rear is overcrowded with horses of identical style — a structurally difficult ask. Even if one gets clear, the fading-in-finish flags on Watty Show, Walkmethroughit, and Ixigreczed make a clean, sustained finish unlikely, and the probability is discounted accordingly.

watchPoints.text: Mercurial Sea sets the pace from the front alone — watch whether he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged or if Hurricane Honey or Island McCoo press him early, as that single factor determines whether this is a made race for front-runner or a gift to the prominent pack.

Island McCoo ran just 14 days ago and carries strong Good-ground form over this trip — watch his position from the first fence; if he settles comfortably in second or third, he is structurally the most dangerous horse in the race for Mercurial Sea.

Love Like This is one of three John Patrick Ryan runners (alongside Ferdia and Kilashee) who all ran seven days ago — watch for any signs of a yard double-banking, as Ryan's representative with the most prominent running style is Love Like This and he may receive the tactical ride.

The rear of the field is structurally congested with redistributed hold-up horses — watch for interference and traffic problems from the fourth-last fence inward, as Watty Show, Ferdia, Kilashee, and Ixigreczed all converge in the same ground with nowhere obvious to go.

Battle Of Benburb returns from 109 days off with course form and a tongue-tie — watch his jumping in the early stages; if he travels fluently and settles behind the lead group, the layoff concern diminishes and he becomes a quiet each-way player in a weak-topped handicap.
